#Expert_Opinion 775#Regulation🔰The Slaughter of the Concept of Regulation🔍Amirhossein Ghalandari, senior researcher at the Regulation Group, has written a note about the recent ruling of the General Assembly of the Administrative Court of Justice regarding the annulment of Resolution 473 of the Competition Council:🔹The recent ruling of the General Assembly of the Administrative Court of Justice regarding the annulment of Resolution 473 of the Competition Council appears to be a legal dispute in the automobile market; but behind it lies a bigger question: What has happened to regulation in Iran's governance system? The issue is not just a resolution or an institution, but the position that regulation has not yet found in the country.🔸Regulation came to create stability, but in Iran, the regulator's authority is unstable; it came for impartial arbitration, but role conflicts persist; it came to curb market power, but it lacks resources itself; and it came for expert decision-making, but its decisions are subject to political and institutional interventions. When we strip regulation of these characteristics, the issue is no longer a few scattered dysfunctions; the issue is the slaughter of the very concept of regulation.📌Read the full text on the think tank's website. 🗞️Published in: Farhikhtegan newspaper💠Sharif Governance Think Tank |Website| |Telegram Channel| |Bale Channel| |Rubika Channel| |Instagram|
